en: "Well, y'know, if you can't pay the fee, maybe I'll have you pay with your body...{w}is what I was thinking!"{w}
note: Editorial: removed the doubled 'I figured ... is what I was thinking'; 'y'know' keeps y'see for the Leprechaun.

en: "What are you going to do, mogu?{w}N-no, stop it, moguuu!?"{w}

note: Source splits shinasai mid-word with effort; English splits the command the same way.

en: "GYAAAAAH!!{w}O-ow! Ow! That hurts, moguuu!!{w}What are you thinking, moguuu!?"{w}

note: tashuke = slurred, cut-off tasuke(te); kept as a slurred, interrupted 'help'. | Proof: no cut-off mark, the source has none (lead rule).
rameee = slurred dame; rendered as slurred 'please' after 'No'.

en: Before long, Jera came back out from the depths, beaming with satisfaction.{w}
"Ufufu, so cuuute~{w}So anyway, here's my fee. I got myself some whiskers!"{w}
note: Raizam's gender unknown: no pronoun for the whiskers' owner.

en: "S-so cruel... So cruel, mogu...{w}My precious whiskers and all... *sniff*"{w}
The leak in the cave was fixed.{w}
note: No subject in source (Jera did the repair); passive used.

en: "Mmm, so comfy, mogu!{w}She was kind of a you-know-what in lots of ways, but she sure knows her stuff, mogu!"{w}
note: Are na hito = 'a you-know-what'; Jera picks the word up in 4282. Jera is female per glossary.
Jera overhears Raizam.

en: "MOGEH!?{w}Th-th-that means... um...{w}A w-wonderful big sis, mogu!!"{w}
note: Editorial: 'big sis' echoes Jera's self-reference in 4253 (slice_033), so her 'That's more like it~' lands.

en: Digging onward, you came out into a somewhat open space.{w}The cool air feels pleasant.{w}{p}It seems surprisingly comfortable to live in.{w}...Especially for, say, a mole.{w}
note: Proof: ongoing states in the present (lead convention), as in the twin row 4185 (slice_033).
Glossary form; 20 chars, over the ~16 name-box guide. Check fit in game.
Leprechaun = 'him' (jijii, glossary male).

en:
"Damn, where'd he go...{w}Hey! If you see him, you'd better tell me, got it!?
Don't you dare go behind my back!!"{w}

"Oh dear, oh dear, oh dear...{w}This has turned into a terrible mess..."{w}{p}"Eek!?"{w}{p}"Wh-why, you gave me a fright.{w}If you folks see a greedy-looking thief,
don't tell 'em where I am..."{w}
note: Trails off: the thief interrupts (2662). Thief's gender unknown -> 'em.

en: "H-help me, I beg ya~...{w}Let me go, won'tcha~~~!!"{w}
note: Rustic old-man speech (kunro) kept as folksy contractions.

en:
"Heh, now that I know where the Leprechaun is,
I've got no more use for you lot.{w}All right, you dogs! Get 'em!!"{w}
note: yaro-domo (gang address) rendered 'you dogs' to keep the roughness without assigning gender. | Proof: 'All right' spelling (corpus norm, as 2804).

en: "G-good adventurers, you did splendidly!{w}I'll be in your debt for the rest of my liiiife~"{w}
note: Editorial: you've done right by me -> you did splendidly (closer to yoku yatte kudasatta).

en: "Ah, that's right, I must give you something as thanks.{w}Hmmm...{w}Then how about I share some of my treasure?"{w}{p}"I can't give you all of it, but just a little bit..."{w}

"My prized statue's in there too,
so take a good long look at it later.{w}...Heh heh heh."{w}{p}"Well then, take care of yourselves..."{w}
note: mufufu = sly chuckle -> 'Heh heh heh' (cf. old-man statue in slice 023).

en:
"Oh dear, oh dear, oh dear...{w}This has turned into a terrible mess..."{w}{p}"Eek!?"{w}{p}"Wh-why, you gave me a fright.{w}If you folks see a greedy-looking thief,
don't tell 'em where I am, would ya?"{w}
note: Full (uninterrupted) version of 2660.

en:
"Oh dear, oh dear, oh dear...{w}This has turned into a terrible mess..."{w}{p}"Eek!?"{w}{p}"Wh-why, you gave me a fright.{w}Y'see, a friend of mine with some treasure
has been targeted by thieves and is being chased..."{w}
note: Editorial: untangled 'who's got treasure got marked by thieves'; kept identical to 2771 up to the interruption.

en: "W-wait, I don't have any treasure!"{w}{p}"I'm a dummy!{w}A dummy geezer!!{w}You picked a dud, better luck next tiiime!!"{w}
note: hazure, zannen deshita = carnival 'you lose' patter.

en:
"Huh?{w}Hmph... now that you mention it,
your beard does sit kinda different, huh?"{w}

"Fine...{w}In that case,
you can take me to the one who's got the treasure!"{w}
"Ah! Damn, he got away!{w}Can't be helped, I'll try somewhere else...{w}You lot better keep looking too, got it!?"{w}

note: Editorial: same fix as 2752 (interrupted twin). Friend's gender unknown: no pronoun.

en:
There were two people, happily poking each other's cheeks
and frolicking together.{w}
note: Editorial: 'playing around' reads as cheating in English; jarete iru = frolicking.

en: Not wanting to spoil the moment, you left.{w}
note: Editorial: 'left the spot so as not to' was stiff. Source has the common miswriting mizu wo sasu (spoil the mood).

en: There was a Werebeast, head hung low.{w}As you quietly watched...{w}...your eyes met!{w}
note: Editorial: second sentence aligned with the parallel row 2884 (slice_035); 'to see what was wrong' dropped. Guld (gender unknown): no pronoun.

en: Guld came to you in tears.{w}
note: nakitsukareta: subject restored as Guld (speaker of 2788/2791).

en: "P-please teach me Strafe Pursuit~{w}Then I'll be head over heels for Honey...{w}...Huh? Well, anyway, the forest will be at peace!"{w}
note: Editorial: 'head over heels' echoes 2886 (slice_035, 'Honey will be head over heels for me'), so the reversed slip reads as one. Guld's muddle (boku ga Honey ni meromero) kept as written.
Editorial: aligned with the parallel prompt 2887 'Teach Guld Pursuit?' (slice_035). 26 chars.

en:
"No! Don't!
Don't be so mean to me!"{w}
note: Reply to 'No'.
Reply to 'Yes'.

en: "How can this be!?{w}This person doesn't have Strafe Pursuit!"{w}
note: Editorial: aligned with the parallel row 2894 (slice_035). kono hito: selected party member, gender unknown.

en: "Thank you! Let's start the lesson-sson right away!"{w}
note: Editorial: restores sassoku (right away) and matches 2896 (slice_035); ressun-sun kept as the playful 'lesson-sson'.

en: "All right! Now I'm a Strafe Pursuit user too!"{w}
note: Editorial: matches 2899 (slice_035).

en:
"You learned Strafe Pursuit!
You're wonderful, Guld!"{w}
"Thank you, Honey! Thank you, everyone!{w}Now I'm a full-fledged High Master Ranger too!"{w}
note: Editorial: 'Thanks, Honey! Everyone!' was clipped; matches 2903 (slice_035). High Master (Elm3/glossary note), Ranger = Elm3 glossary value for kariudo; class name still open (2903 says 'hunter').

en: "Oh, look! The Rampaging Elephants are coming!"{w}
note: Plural: the elephants answer in a chorus (2816).
Editorial: chant aligned with Honey's 2856 (slice_035). Line break kept.
Glossary form; 18 chars, over the ~16 name-box guide. Check fit in game.
